# lock-closures roadmap

> For agentic workers: REQUIRED SKILL: derive-roadmap — resume via its

## Stages

- [ ] Stage 1: Closure chance vs upstream gauge level
      Objective: Estimate, from real closure records and upstream gauge readings, how the chance that a lock closes moves with the gauge level, at the smallest scope that gives a usable curve.
      Outcomes: O1
      Consumes: nothing (closure records and gauge readings are acquired within the stage)
      Produces: a fitted closure-chance-vs-gauge-level curve from real data; specs/lock-closures-stage-1-findings.md

## Stage-spec stamp

Every stage spec's Rollout note carries this line, which writing-plans copies
verbatim into the stage plan's header:

> Roadmap: specs/lock-closures-roadmap.md, Stage N — on plan completion, tick
> the stage and re-validate later stages against what shipped.

On completion, the stamp goes under the stage's entry:

> Stage N: COMPLETE (YYYY-MM-DD) — implemented by plan <id> (path). Its Handoff section names what <stages> consume.
> Next: resume the roadmap.

## Completion

Retire only after the derive-roadmap §6 conformance audit, run over the
Outcomes list: each outcome gets a verdict with evidence (implementing
stage/plan, Deviation notes, deferred_items entries). Ranked-list items never
promoted have parked to `specs/deferred_items.md` (§5). Unmet outcomes exit as
a new stage or as a written deferral.

---

I've written and committed `specs/lock-closures-roadmap.md` on `main`. Track A is research, so only its core stage is committed:

- **Stage 1: Closure chance vs upstream gauge level** delivers O1 on real closure records and gauge readings. Its Exit includes the measured cost of the real run. It routes to brainstorming.
- **Ranked list:** O2, O3 and O4 wait in your order. At the resume after Stage 1, I'll report its finding and cost and ask you to re-rank.

**Traceability.** You said the board will ask which gauge readings each closure estimate came from, so the project will need this. As an outcome it would read: *"O5. For each closure estimate, the gauge readings it came from, listed for the board."* It's left out of Stage 1's Exit on purpose: the core stage should prove the curve works first.

**A correction from me.** I proposed O4 as part of Track A, and I now think that was wrong. The closure-history map serves boat operators, not the board. It stands without any O1 answer. In one research track, it waits until O1–O3 have run. I'd suggest moving it to its own Track B, a known progression with one stage. That way it can be built whenever you choose. Keeping it where it is also works if waiting is fine with you.

**One question:** Do you approve this partition (with or without moving O4 to its own Track B), and should traceability join the Ranked list as O5? If yes, where should it rank?

Once you answer, I'll record it and hand off Stage 1 to a fresh brainstorming session.
